chapters.title: Chapter 3: TDS on Investment Income and Other Payments

lessons.title: TDS on Dividends, Mutual Fund Payouts and EPF Withdrawals

body.text: Dividends and mutual fund payouts are taxed at your slab rate, but TDS only starts once a single company or fund pays you more than ₹10,000 in a year. EPF withdrawals are the opposite: the TDS is usually avoidable if you plan the exit.

children.text: Sameer, 35, a chartered accountant in Pune, holds a portfolio of dividend-paying shares in his Zerodha account and an IDCW option in a mutual fund. When he checked his AIS for tax year 2026-27, he found dividends from four companies but TDS from only two of them. Many of his clients ask the same questions every year, along with a third: what happens to TDS when they withdraw their EPF? This lesson covers the three most common investment payouts that attract TDS and what each one really costs.

markDefs.definition: Each company that pays you a dividend applies the threshold only to the dividends it pays you in the tax year. Dividends from different companies are not added together for TDS.

children.text: Since dividend distribution tax was abolished in 2020, dividends are taxed in the shareholder's hands at slab rates. TDS on dividends now sits in Section 393(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, Table, Sl. No. 7 (formerly Section 194). The company paying the dividend is the deductor, so the threshold is tested

body.caption: TDS on dividends for resident individuals, tax year 2026-27

cells: No TDS if dividends paid electronically by that company to you in the year total ₹10,000 or less
Added to your income and taxed at your slab rate, whatever the TDS
Interest on money borrowed to buy shares
From tax year 2026-27, no deduction at all against dividend income. The earlier limit of 20% of dividends was removed by the Finance Act, 2026
Avoiding TDS if your tax is nil
Submit Form 121 (formerly Forms 15G and 15H) to the company or its registrar

children.text: Sameer is in the 20% slab of the old regime. His tax on ₹51,500 of dividends is ₹51,500 × 20% × 1.04 = ₹10,712. With only ₹3,600 deducted, he still owes ₹7,112. The dividends of ₹9,500 and ₹6,000 that had no TDS are just as taxable as the rest.

body.title: Quick Check: Why No TDS From the Bank Stock?
body.question: Sameer received ₹9,500 of dividends from the private sector bank and no TDS was deducted. Which statement is correct?
options: Bank dividends are exempt from tax
The company's dividends to him stayed within the ₹10,000 threshold, but the dividend is still taxable at his slab rate
His total dividends across all companies were below ₹10,000
The company forgot to deduct and will recover it next year
body.explanation: The threshold is tested per company. That bank paid him ₹9,500, which is within ₹10,000, so no TDS applied. His total dividends of ₹51,500 are irrelevant for TDS, but every rupee is taxable income and appears in his AIS.

body.text: If you hold shares bought with a loan against securities or margin funding, the interest you pay can no longer be deducted from dividend income, starting tax year 2026-27. Leveraged dividend strategies that relied on that deduction now cost more.

children.text: Share Buybacks: Out of the Dividend Net Again
Buybacks have been taxed three different ways in less than two years, and the TDS treatment changed each time.

body.title: How buyback proceeds have been taxed

events.title: Company pays buyback tax
events.description: The company paid a separate tax on the buyback. Shareholders received the proceeds tax-free and there was no TDS.

events.title: Taxed as dividend
events.description: The entire buyback amount was treated as a dividend in the shareholder's hands, taxed at slab rates with 10% TDS. The cost of the shares became a capital loss.

events.title: Taxed as capital gains
events.description: The Finance Act, 2026 treats only the gain (buyback price minus cost) as capital gains, at normal equity rates. Dividend TDS no longer applies. Promoters face an additional tax.

body.title: Tendering 10 shares bought at ₹3,000 into a buyback at ₹4,000, held over 12 months

columns.label: Buyback in March 2026 (dividend rules)
points: Capital loss of ₹30,000 to set off against capital gains, now or in later years

columns.label: Buyback in September 2026 (capital gains rules)
points: TDS: nil for a resident shareholder
Tax: nil if total equity long-term gains for the year stay within the ₹1,25,000 exemption, otherwise 12.5% on the excess
No artificial capital loss to track

children.text: Mutual Fund Payouts: IDCW vs Growth

markDefs.definition: Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal. A mutual fund option that pays out part of the scheme's value periodically. The payout is taxed like a dividend at your slab rate, not as capital gains.

children.text: When a mutual fund pays out under the
, the fund house deducts TDS under Section 393(1), Table, Sl. No. 4(i) (formerly Section 194K): 10% once its payouts to you exceed

in the tax year. Redeeming units is different. Selling or redeeming mutual fund units, including through a systematic withdrawal plan, produces capital gains, and resident investors face no TDS on it at all.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Redemptions
body.textWithBlank: A resident investor who redeems equity mutual fund units at a profit suffers ___ TDS on the redemption.
body.explanation: TDS under the mutual fund provision covers income distributed on units, such as IDCW. Capital gains on redemption are excluded for residents. Non-resident investors are a different story and do face TDS on redemption gains.

children.text: Meena, 52, a doctor in Jaipur in the 30% slab, receives ₹1,20,000 a year as IDCW payouts from a balanced advantage fund. Compare that with taking the same ₹1,20,000 as long-term gains by redeeming units of the growth option.

body.title: Meena's ₹1,20,000 a year: IDCW payout vs growth option redemption

children.text: The IDCW payout suffers ₹12,000 of TDS and ₹37,440 of tax in total. The growth option route suffers no TDS, and if the fund is equity-oriented for tax, the units were held over 12 months and she has no other long-term equity gains that year, ₹1,20,000 of gains falls within the ₹1,25,000 exemption and attracts no tax. For a high-slab investor, the option chosen matters far more than the TDS.

body.title: Try It: Meena's Bill at Filing
body.prompt: Meena's fund house deducted ₹12,000 on ₹1,20,000 of IDCW payouts. In the 30% slab with 4% cess, how much more tax does she owe on these payouts when she files her return?
body.explanation: Total tax is ₹1,20,000 × 30% × 1.04 = ₹37,440. After ₹12,000 of TDS, she owes ₹25,440. Because that exceeds ₹10,000, it should really be paid as advance tax during the year.

children.text: You met this in the job-switch lesson. Here are the full rules in one place, because EPF is often the largest single sum a young professional ever withdraws.

cells: Withdrawal after 5 or more years of continuous service, counting service with earlier employers whose balance was transferred
No TDS, and the withdrawal is generally tax-free
Withdrawal before 5 years, amount ₹50,000 or less
No TDS, though parts of it may still be taxable
Withdrawal before 5 years, amount above ₹50,000, valid PAN linked to UAN
Withdrawal before 5 years because of ill-health, closure of the employer's business or other reasons beyond your control
Generally not taxable, so no TDS
Form 121 submitted because total tax for the year is nil
Interest on your own contributions above ₹2.5 lakh a year
Taxable each year, and the EPFO deducts TDS on that interest

body.title: Scenario: Anita Leaves for Her MBA
body.scenario: Anita, 27, worked for 3.5 years at a Hyderabad IT firm and resigned in June 2026 to start a two-year full-time MBA. Her EPF balance is ₹3,20,000. Apart from ₹2,40,000 of salary for April and May, she will have no income this tax year. She plans to withdraw her EPF to pay fees.
body.prompt: Will TDS be deducted, can she avoid it, and is there an option she should consider before withdrawing?
body.modelAnswer: Her service is under five years and the amount is above ₹50,000, so the EPFO would deduct 10%, ₹32,000, if her PAN is linked. Because she is withdrawing early for a reason within her control, the employer contributions and interest become taxable. But her total income for the year, even including the taxable portion of the withdrawal, is very likely within the new regime's ₹12,00,000 rebate limit, so her tax for the year should be nil. She can therefore submit Form 121 with her withdrawal claim to prevent the TDS altogether. If she forgets, she can still claim the ₹32,000 back as a refund in her return. Before withdrawing, she should also consider leaving the balance untouched: EPF accounts continue to earn interest for a period after you stop contributing, and if she rejoins employment after the MBA and transfers the account, her earlier service still counts towards five years.

body.title: Review Dividends, Payouts and EPF
steps: Download your dividend statement from your broker's back-office, such as Zerodha Console, for tax year 2026-27
Group dividends by company and note which crossed ₹10,000 and suffered TDS
Check whether any mutual fund you hold is in an IDCW option, and whether the growth option would suit you better
Estimate tax on all dividends and IDCW at your slab rate, and plan advance tax if the shortfall after TDS exceeds ₹10,000
Log in to the EPFO member portal, confirm your PAN is linked to your UAN, and check your years of continuous service
Match every dividend and payout against your AIS before filing

body.label: Zerodha Console
body.description: Zerodha's back-office. The Reports section includes a dividend statement and tax P&L for your holdings. Other brokers offer similar reports.

cards.definition: TDS on dividends. 10% above ₹10,000 per company per tax year. Formerly Section 194.
TDS on income from mutual fund units, such as IDCW. 10% above ₹10,000. Formerly Section 194K.
Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal. Mutual fund payouts taxed at your slab rate, with TDS.
Taxed as capital gains on the actual gain, not as a dividend. No dividend TDS.
TDS at 10% on EPF withdrawals above ₹50,000 before five years of service. Formerly Section 192A.
Provision under which no interest expenditure is deductible against dividend or mutual fund income from tax year 2026-27.

points: Dividends attract 10% TDS only once a single company pays you more than ₹10,000 in a tax year, but all dividends are taxable at your slab rate
From tax year 2026-27, interest on borrowings cannot be deducted from dividend or mutual fund income
Buybacks from 1 April 2026 are taxed as capital gains on the actual gain, so dividend TDS no longer applies to them
IDCW payouts suffer 10% TDS above ₹10,000 per fund house, while redemptions by residents suffer no TDS
EPF withdrawals before five years and above ₹50,000 attract 10% TDS under Section 392(7), which Form 121 can prevent if your tax is nil
For high-slab investors, choosing growth over IDCW, or transferring EPF instead of withdrawing, saves far more than managing TDS
